answer: Prompt architecture, concept art, vector assets, inpainting and colour: the still image made with diffusion models.

children.name: Prompt Architecture and Style Replication
children.blurb: Prompt architecture is the structured design of text and parameter inputs that steer a generative image model toward a specific visual outcome.

children.name: Concept Art and World-Building
children.blurb: Concept art and world-building in generative illustration covers early visual exploration of characters, environments, props, and cultures for games, film, animation, and interactive media.

children.name: Vector Graphics and Interface Assets
children.blurb: Vector graphics and interface assets cover scalable two-dimensional artwork built from paths, points, curves, and fills rather than pixels.

children.name: Inpainting and Canvas Expansion
children.blurb: Inpainting and canvas expansion are two related techniques in generative illustration.

children.name: Algorithmic Colour Grading
children.blurb: Algorithmic colour grading refers to the use of software models to adjust hue, saturation, luminance, contrast, and colour balance across a still image or video sequence.

sections.body: This field is the practical use of diffusion models to produce still images for visual art and design. It covers writing prompts that steer a model toward a particular look, generating concept sketches, producing vector-style assets, repairing or extending an image, and adjusting colour. The work is not theoretical; artists and designers now use these tools daily to make backgrounds, character sheets, interface elements and finished illustrations. The site tracks 1000 live image generation models, and this section draws on that catalogue to explain what each technique actually does.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The basic generation of a single image from a text prompt is largely solved for common subjects and styles, but consistency across a series remains hard. Concept art benefits from fast iteration, yet models still struggle with exact perspective, repeated characters and fine text. Inpainting and canvas expansion work well for small fixes and simple extensions, but large structural changes often introduce seams or lose context. Vector graphics and interface assets are only partly automated; models can suggest shapes and layouts, but clean, editable vector output usually needs manual cleanup. Algorithmic colour grading is reliable for broad adjustments, though matching a specific film or brand palette still requires careful prompting and checking. The honest limit is that these tools assist a skilled person, they do not replace judgement about composition, legibility or taste.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader who wants to control the look of an image should start with Prompt Architecture and Style Replication, which explains how wording, order and reference terms shape output. Concept Art and World-Building then shows how to use those prompts for environments, characters and props across a project. Vector Graphics and Interface Assets moves from raster art to the harder problem of clean lines and scalable output for apps and print. Inpainting and Canvas Expansion covers fixing mistakes and extending a frame after the first generation, which is often where a piece actually gets finished. Algorithmic Colour Grading sits last because it assumes an image already exists and needs a consistent mood or palette applied. Together the five pages follow a working order: describe, build, refine, repair, and grade.
